What the numbers say

For the session of Tuesday, November 10, 2026, the DappGo regime model reads the tracked universe (36 US-listed stocks and ETFs on DappGo's reviewed watchlist) as risk-off. SPY is below its 50-day average and above its 200-day average; its 20-day trend is down and realised volatility is in the moderate band.

10 of 36 tickers (28%) are priced above their own 20-day moving average, and 17 of 34 (50%) above their 200-day average. Below 30% is the level the model treats as weak breadth, which is enough on its own for a risk-off reading. On the day 7 rose and 28 fell, with 1 unchanged; the median move was −1.42%.

Among sectors with at least two tracked names, Healthcare had the strongest average move at −0.90% and Technology the weakest at −2.51%, a spread of 1.61 percentage points. The standard deviation of sector averages was 2.06 points; a larger figure means sectors moved less in step.

3 tickers have a 14-day RSI at or below 30 (NVDA, INTC, SNDK), and none is at or above 70. An RSI extreme records how one-sided recent trading has been. It is not, by itself, evidence that the move is about to reverse.

Against the previous session in this archive (2026-11-09), the share of tickers above the 20-day average moved from 36% to 28%, and the regime reading changed from mixed to risk-off.
